Vitamin B12 deficiency is one of the most common undiagnosed deficiency conditions in today's date.

It occurs when the body does not get enough vitamin B12 through our diet, an essential nutrient for healthy nerves, red blood cells, and DNA production. 

Common symptoms include: 
- fatigue
- generalised weakness 
- numbness or tingling in the hands and feet, 
- memory problems
- irritability
- hair loss

It may result from poor dietary intake, especially in strict vegetarians, or from conditions that reduce absorption, such as certain stomach or intestinal disorders. 

Diagnosis is made through blood tests. Treatment includes dietary changes, oral supplements, or injections depending on the severity.

If you are suffering from any of the above symptoms, consult Dr.Ajinkya Achalare for an expert opinion and complete orthopedic care.

SHOULDER DISLOCATION

A shoulder dislocation occurs when the ball of the upper arm bone comes out of its socket completely. 

It can happen after a fall, road traffic accident or during a contact sport. 

Patients experience sudden onset severe pain, difficulty in moving the arm and a visible deformity around the shoulder. 

Emergency care by an orthopaedic surgeon is required as it must be reduced back into its position.

Once the joint is reduced, proper rehabilitation is essential to restore strength and movement. Most of the patients do well later.

Rarely in cases of repeated dislocations, a key-hole arthroscopic surgery is required to repair the torn tissue.

If you are suffering from repeated dislocations of shoulder, consult Dr.Ajinkya Achalare for expert advice and complete orthpedic care.

PLANTAR FASCIITIS 

Heel pain is one of the commonest orthopedic complaints faced by millions of people worldwide and plantar fasciitis is the leading cause.

It can affect anyone who needs to stand or walk for long hours at work or for any other reason.

If you are experiencing persistent heel pain, then this blog will answer many of your doubts.

Tennis elbow or Lateral Epicondylitis is a common cause of elbow pain.

It is caused by overuse of the forearm muscles and hence the tendons that attach on the outer side of the elbow. 

Despite its name, it does not affect only tennis players but it can affect anyone who performs repetitive gripping, lifting, typing, or wrist movements. 

Symptoms include pain and tenderness on the outer elbow, reduced grip strength, and discomfort while lifting objects or shaking hands. 

Most patients improve with activity modification, ice fomentation, anti-inflammatory medications and stretching exercises. 
Rarely PRP injection and surgery are used as the last resorts.

Early treatment helps prevent chronic pain and allows a quicker return to daily activities and sports.

If you are suffering from constant elbow pain, consult Dr.Ajinkya Achalare for expert orthopedic care.

Jumper’s Knee (Patellar Tendinopathy)

Jumper’s knee is an overuse injury affecting the tendon connecting the knee cap (patella) to the shin bone (tibia). 

It commonly occurs in athletes involved in jumping sports such as basketball, volleyball, and athletics. 

Patients typically experience pain at the front of the knee, especially during jumping, running, squatting, or climbing stairs. 

Early treatment includes activity modification, ice application, and physiotherapy focused on strengthening the quadriceps and tendon. Ignoring symptoms can lead to chronic pain and reduced performance. 

Timely diagnosis and appropriate rehabilitation are essential for a successful recovery.

If you are suffering from similar symptoms, consult Dr.Ajinkya Achalare for an expert orthopedic advice and care.

Para-Meniscal Cyst of Knee: sign of an underlying meniscus tear

A para-meniscal cyst is a fluid-filled swelling that develops next to the meniscus (C-shaped cushion inside the knee joint)

It usually occurs when joint fluid escapes through a small meniscal tear and collects outside the meniscus. 

Patients notice a localised bump near the knee along with pain, tenderness, and discomfort during activities likje walking, climbing stairs. 

MRI is the best investigation to confirm the diagnosis and identify the associated meniscal tear. 

Treatment depends on severity and duration of symptoms and includes medicines & physiotherapy to arthroscopic (key-hole) surgery to repair the underlying meniscus tear and prevent recurrence of the cyst.

If you are suffering from persistent knee pain or a localised swelling along the knee joint, consult Dr.Ajinkya Achalare for an expert orthopedic care.

METATARSALGIA : FOREFOOT PAIN

Metatarsalgia is a common condition causing pain and inflammation in the ball of the foot, usually beneath the metatarsal bones. 

It often develops due to excessive walking, running, high-impact sports, improper footwear, foot deformities, or being overweight. 

Patients typically experience a burning, aching, or sharp pain that worsens while standing or walking and improves with rest. 

Early treatment includes activity modification, orthotic insoles, stretching exercises, and anti-inflammatory medications fora short course. 

However identifying and addressing the underlying cause is essential to prevent chronic symptoms and restore comfortable, pain-free mobility.

If you are suffering from pain over the forefoot, consult Dr.Ajinkya Achalare for best orthopedic advice and care!

WRIST SPRAIN is an injury caused by stretching or tearing of the ligaments that support the wrist joint.

It commonly occurs after a fall on an outstretched hand, twisting injury or lifting weights at the gym or during a sport. 

Symptoms include sudden pain, swelling, bruising, tenderness, and difficulty moving the wrist or gripping objects. 

Immediate care includes rest to the joint, ice application, compression with a crepe bandage, elevation, and temporary splint support. 

Persistent pain and/or swelling beyond 1-2 days should not be ignored and needs urgent medical attention.

If you are have sustained a wrist injury, consult Dr.Ajinkya Achalare at Sphere Clinic, Parel East, Mumbai for expert advice and care.

HYALURONIC ACID INJECTION

A major cause of knee pain in old age is knee osteoarthritis, a degenerative condition in which the smooth cartilage lining of the knee gradually wears out. 

While physiotherapy, weight management, and medications help most of the patients, some continue to have persistent symptoms. 

In such cases, hyaluronic acid injections can be considered as a safe and effective non-surgical treatment option.

If you are suffering from arthritic knee pain, consult Dr.Ajinkya Achalare at Sphere Clinic, Parel for an expert advice and care.

CALCIUM SUPPLEMENTS IN ELDERLY 

- As we age, calcium absorption through gut reduces, increasing the risk of osteoporosis (weak bones) and fractures. 

- In women, this risk further increases due to hormonal changes.

- Elder individuals benefit from calcium supplements when dietary intake is inadequate. 

- The preferred supplements are calcium citrate and calcium carbonate. 

- Calcium citrate is better absorbed in people with low stomach acid and causes less bloating, making it suitable for older adults. 

- Calcium carbonate is economical and works best when taken with meals. 

- Most elderly patients require 1000–1200 mg of elemental calcium daily along with adequate vitamin D for proper absorption. 

- Although excessive calcium intake is hazardous and should be avoided. It is advisable to take supplements only as per your doctor's advice.

- Remember! Calcium supplements are always complementary to a balanced diet and can not replace it.
